rules_for_all_cases: Follow dataset-plan.md §5 (construction), §5.2 (distractors), §6 (realism), §7 (leakage) and the avoid rules of §10.2.
'documents' counts distinct documents (document IDs), including any out-of-window document, normal report or unsigned document; versions are not counted.
Every document version and record version from 2 onward has a realistic, non-null reason that reveals nothing.

Out-of-window document: its documentation date and every date it mentions lie outside Day 0 to Day +28. Its neurological observation is a Grade 0 assessment (e.g. ICE 10/10) or an excluded symptom (e.g. tremor), never a qualifying finding or a free symptom word.

Extra (random) amendment: changes no neurological content, no sedating drug and no event time (e.g. a corrected vital sign). In a case with a multi-version record it is documented before record version 1.

Extra record versions use only the allowed patterns of §5.1: 'same values re-entered'; 'corrected to agreeing value' (only on the named 7.7 field, with every record version recorded after the last document, so 7.6 condition (c) fails); 'change still disagrees' (Pos only, on the named discrepancy field).
Normal EEG or imaging report: plainly normal, inside the window, not near a finding in a way that could read as a conflicting assessment.

Extra 'not assessable' period: a non-sedation reason (e.g. off the unit for a scan); after the documented onset; not on the day of the documented maximum grade; not on the record's onset date; at least 2 calendar days from any qualifying finding; applies only to its own documentation date.
Unsigned extra: contains no neurological observation and no sedating drug. An 'unsigned later version' differs from its signed version only in non-neurological content.
No sedating drug in the same note as any finding, or in the 24 hours before it, unless the scenario needs one (A30).

Free symptom words for cognition or speech (e.g. 'confused', 'word-finding difficulty') only where 'ungradeable_symptom' is 'required', in a note with no ICE total and no consciousness description, on a calendar day with no ICE assessment (NEW-13, NEW-14).
Consciousness wording clearly fits one Table 6 category or is plainly normal, except in SC-23 (NEW-15).

No relative-time range phrase ('overnight', 'last night') in a note documented on Day 0 or Day +29 (NEW-16); no competing cause in the same note as, or within 2 calendar days before, a finding dated by a range (NEW-17).
Style 'with typos': typos never change numbers, scores, dates or times, negations, or the words of any observation the intended answer relies on.
No death except SC-69; no CAPD except SC-55; no record Grade 5 except SC-56; no age under 18 except SC-54; no baseline developmental delay anywhere.

Note v1 supports G2; amended v2 (signed, current) supports G1; record G2
Record G4 rests on a raised-ICP sign found only in the source text, not Table 6; Table 6 findings G2
Record says no ICANS; no formal assessment at all (narrative notes only); no qualifying finding. Distractor: an ungradeable neurological symptom
Record onset 2 days late
Two assessments within the same hour disagree, and the disagreement decides the grade; one reading matches the record, the other does not, so the readings lead to different categories
Typical course recorded correctly: first finding Day +5 (ICE 9), worst Day +6 (ICE 4, awakens to voice); record onset Day +5, G2
Record G1; the earliest finding is Grade 2 without doubt; a later finding would be Grade 3 but has a documented competing cause and no clinician statement. Readings G2 or G3 both give 7.2

briefs.scenario: Adult case with a CAPD assessment in a note
Same pattern; record correctly says G3

Record says no ICANS; formal Grade 0 assessments; no qualifying finding; a documented "not assessable" period stated explicitly (e.g. "ICE not done, intubated and sedated"). Distractor: an ungradeable neurological symptom
Record says no ICANS; notes document qualifying ICANS (no competing cause)

Record says ICANS; notes contain only ungradeable symptoms (e.g. "confused", no ICE or consciousness level), including on the record's onset date, with no gradeable assessment that day; no "not assessable" period (with one, the grade would be 7.4: A22 as amended)

briefs.scenario: ICE alone gives the wrong grade: ICE 8 plus awakens only to touch, no sedation; record follows ICE (G1)
A consciousness phrase that could fit two categories decides the grade; one reading matches the record, the other does not, so the readings lead to different categories
Onset finding with no event time in the note; record uses the documentation date
Same finding in a nursing note (evening) and restated in next morning's physician note; record uses the earlier date

Late-signed EEG report: seizure on Day +7, report signed Day +10; record G2 on Day +8, revised to G3 on Day +10. The report's `documented_at` is after the Day +8 record version and no later than the revision
Amendment adds a higher-grade finding; record not updated. Counterpart of SC-63

Two assessments within the same hour disagree on the earliest day (one meets a Grade 1 criterion, one is a formal Grade 0 assessment); record onset is the next day, from an unambiguous finding. Readings: onset that day (record +1, 7.1) or the next day (7.7)
Recorded onset date has "awakens spontaneously" with no drowsiness and ICE 10 (Grade 0); first qualifying finding next day; grade correct
Recorded onset date has only an excluded symptom (tremor or headache), no gradeable assessment that day
briefs.expected_onset: 7.4 + record date matches an excluded or sub-threshold symptom

briefs.scenario: One clear ICE score (G2) is the only abnormal finding; record says G1
Sedated, documented "not assessable" on some days; record G4; all assessed days support G2

Recorded onset date has only a sub-threshold symptom (e.g. word-finding difficulty, no ICE, no consciousness description), so the case carries the "ungradeable neurological symptom" flag. The grade answer depends on NEW-12 (§10.2) and is marked so
briefs.expected_onset: 7.4 + record date matches an excluded or sub-threshold symptom

briefs.scenario: A clinician attributes a finding to another cause; the record counts it
Onset finding observed before midnight (explicit date and time in text), note documented after midnight; record uses the event date. Counterpart of SC-59
Documented death; record grade 1 to 4 (not 5). The development case documents the death inside the window; the locked case after Day +28

Onset revised after an amended note: a signed amendment adds an earlier, timed finding to an existing note; record onset revised after it. The amendment's `documented_at` is between the two record versions
A late-entry note documents an earlier first finding; record onset revised after it. The late entry's `documented_at` is between the two record versions
Text copied forward into notes after documented resolution, verbatim or with only dates, times or formatting changed (vary across cases); no real recurrence
Record says ICANS; onset left empty; grade correct
Recorded onset date has a narrative normal neuro note (no ICE) as its only assessment. Distractor: an excluded symptom (e.g. headache) is also documented that day
briefs.expected_onset: 7.4 + record date matches an excluded or sub-threshold symptom

briefs.scenario: Record G3; notes support only G2 (ICE 5, awakens to voice); no Grade 3 finding; no documented "not assessable" period

Record says no ICANS; formal Grade 0 assessments in the window; no qualifying finding; no "not assessable" period; distractors such as CRS fever, tremor or headache. ICE 0, unarousable, no competing cause documented; record G3
